text.p: Food group Goodman Fielder Ltd said on Tuesday it has restructured its Steggles poultry business, changing the five existing state-based units into a single national management group.
Goodman Fielder chief executive David Hearn said the changes would provide a better service to major national customers and streamline internal management and administration processes.

"As a result of these changes, and to ensure we have the right team in place for future growth, the management team reporting to Philip Stanton, managing director of Steggles has been restructured," Hearn said.

"This team will comprise Michael Leahy responsible for livestock, Jim McKenzie responsible for processing, Geoff McGeachie responsible for sales, marketing and distribution, Stephen Sasse responsible for human resources and a financial controller, who is yet to be appointed".
"These changes will help us service our major national customers better and make Steggles much more competitive in the future," Hearn said.
He said further details of the new structure were being finalised and it was expected the changes would be in place by mid-April.
While the company had a flat operating profit of A$238.7 million in 1995/96, the poultry division suffered a profit fall to A$9.6 million from A$15.1 million a year earlier.
Divisional sales rose to A$486.5 million from A$462.9 million.
